summary: Owner rules hold: CustomerOrderApi filters Order on customerUserId from loadCaller() with no admin branch and no id/query channel, CheckoutApi stamps customerUserId from optionalCaller() and never from the body, MenuPhotoAdminApi and MenuAdminApi open every method with requireAdmin(), and MenuPhotoApi/MenuApi are public exactly as api-plan.json says. Conventions are clean: loadAsInstance=false and checkPermission=false everywhere, class names differ from table names (MenuPhotoApi/MenuItemPhoto, CustomerOrderApi/Order), post(target, data), segmentsOf(), db.<Table> only, customerUserId @indexed, Blob written as new Blob([buf],{type}) with verify-on-write and delete-on-mismatch, withoutManaged() on every restated MenuItem/Order row, 403 with code everywhere and no 401, no new dependency and no new egress host. run_check lint is green. The one thing this build should fix before publish is a documented sign-up gate that the code does not apply. The QA report's two functional failures (a self-registered password not working on a later sign-in, and the /login password button) are the app owner's defects, not review findings, and are deliberately not listed here.

findings.message: POST /AuthApi/register creates an account without ever consulting config.auth.openSignup(), while the two other account-creating paths in the same file do (request-link at line 171, google at line 248 which answers 403 not_invited). CLAUDE.md §9, written in this same diff, states the opposite — 'refuses unless config.auth.openSignup()' — so the app's own spec and its code disagree about the front door, and the code is the permissive one. api-plan.json currently says signUp: "open", so the deploy writes AUTH_OPEN_SIGNUP=true and nothing is open today that should be closed; the defect is that the gate is absent rather than true. The moment the owner asks to close sign-ups, request-link and google close and register stays wide open. Worse, scripts/customer-accounts-probe.js pins the ungated behaviour on purpose: it sets AUTH_OPEN_SIGNUP=false and asserts the registration still returns 201, so a later session restoring the gate has to break a green suite to do it. Either add the openSignup() check at the top of register() (and relax the probe), or change CLAUDE.md §9 so it describes what the code does — but one line should say one thing.

register() closes the pre-loaded-seat attack for exactly one address (OWNER_EMAIL) and the header explains that case well, but the same shape survives one step further out. Anyone may now register an address nobody has claimed and set a password on it; AdminApi.setRole (resources/AdminApi.js:107) can later promote any existing row to admin, and AuthApi.password now admits any active row carrying a hash. So an attacker who pre-registers an address the owner later promotes holds an admin password on that row. The exposure is narrow — CLAUDE.md says there are no staff logins, promotion is a deliberate admin act, and an invite alone does not change a role — but the mitigation is cheap and belongs with the owner-address check: either refuse password sign-in on a row whose hash predates its promotion, or clear passwordHash in setRole when a row is raised to admin.

register() uses `claim.created` as the uniqueness arbiter ('Two registrations of one address that interleave land on one key ... the loser is told the account exists'), but lib/auth.js's own measured header for claimUserForEmail says precisely the opposite: Harper's create() is a local getSync plus an unconditional commit retry, 'two concurrent claims on one address can both create', and 'a caller must not read created as proof it was first'. Under a true interleave both registrations therefore get 201 and a session, and the second hashPassword overwrites the first. The preceding findUserByEmail check makes a sequential retry safe, so the practical window is two simultaneous sign-ups of the same address and the blast radius is a member account; the comment claiming a guarantee the platform has measured as absent is the part worth correcting.

customerPassword() ships a literal default password ('pizza-preview-demo') that is hashed onto two seeded member accounts. It is not a provider key, the accounts are example.com, the value is overridable with SEED_CUSTOMER_PASSWORD and the header reasons about why the owner gets no seeded credential — so this is noted rather than blocked. Still: it is a working sign-in credential committed to the owner's repository, and now that AuthApi/password admits any row with a hash it is a real one wherever this script is ever run. Prefer requiring SEED_CUSTOMER_PASSWORD (or a per-run random value printed to stdout) over a default that is the same in every checkout.
